subject: Access controls follow-up: RBAC, support access, and break-glass procedures
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@fintrust.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-10T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Access controls follow-up: RBAC, support access, and break-glass procedures

Hi Samantha
great to meet you and Jake on the call earlier. Quick recap and next steps on access controls so we stay aligned with your security team:

- RBAC: Redwood supports role-based policies (org / project / route) and attribute-based scoping. We can provide a recommended role matrix for typical product teams and map those to FinTrust roles.
- Least privilege: token-scoped API keys, ephemeral session keys for support sessions, and fine-grained model/route ACLs.
- Support access / break-glass: we offer audited, time-limited support sessions with customer-triggered approvals and optional customer-owned KMS to encrypt logs. Break-glass can be tied to an on-call escalation workflow and is fully logged in the audit trail.
- Logs & retention: audit logs are configurable; default 90 days for the hosted plan, longer for Dedicated/Private. We can provide SOC2 evidence and retention policy options.
- Data residency: region pinning by request (US/EU/APAC) and private VPC deployments for stricter controls.

Attachments: I attached a preliminary RBAC matrix and our SOC2 summary for your review.

Next steps: can you confirm the list of FinTrust roles that will need access (e.g., security, ops, SRE, product)? Also would FinTrust prefer time-limited support sessions with customer approval or an automated break-glass flow?

I'll loop Michael and Dev to help scope the RBAC mapping and share a draft by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@fintrust.com>

Cc: Jake Porter <jake.porter@fintrust.com>, security@fintrust.com
Date: 2027-10-10T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Access controls follow-up: RBAC, support access, and break-glass procedures

Thanks Marissa
good summary. A few clarifying questions from our security team: 

1) RBAC matrix: can you confirm whether Redwood supports attribute-based constraints (e.g., environment = prod, scope = customer-id) in addition to static roles? Our SREs need to make sure service accounts can be limited to a single customer shard.

2) Break-glass / support: we'd prefer customer-approval first (we trigger and approve) but need an emergency fallback where Redwood can escalate with a break-glass token tied to an audit and two-person escalation. Is that available for Hosted customers or only Dedicated/Private?

3) Audit logs: what fields are logged for support sessions (commands executed, session start/end, user id, IP)? And can logs be exported to our SIEM?

Jake and I can share a short list of roles today (security, platform, SRE, product). If you can send the RBAC draft, we’ll review and propose any changes.

Best,
Samantha
Samantha Lee
Director, Security Engineering
FinTrust

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@fintrust.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-10T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Access controls follow-up: RBAC, support access, and break-glass procedures

Thanks
answers inline below and attached is a slightly expanded RBAC matrix with examples mapped to FinTrust roles.

1) RBAC/attributes: yes
we support attribute-based scoping (resource tags like environment=prod, customer_id, and label-based constraints). You can combine role + attribute filters so service accounts can be limited to a single customer shard. See the RBAC matrix (attached) for examples.

2) Break-glass: for Hosted customers we provide an auditable break-glass workflow that requires two-step approval (customer admin + Redwood on-call) for emergency elevation. For Dedicated/Private we can configure an automated fallback with customer-managed decisioning (webhook to your tooling). We'll document the process and SLA implications.

3) Audit logs: all support sessions record: session id, initiating user, Redwood support engineer, start/end timestamps, IPs, actions taken (API calls and console commands), and a tamper-evident hash. Logs can be exported via S3/Cloud Storage or streamed to your SIEM via a secure connector. Default retention for hosted is 90 days; we can extend to meet your policy.

Next steps:
- Michael / Dev: can you take the RBAC matrix and highlight any gaps vs. FinTrust's role list?
- Samantha / Jake: please upload the FinTrust role list to this thread or paste it here; we'll produce a final mapping and proposed access policies.

I'll schedule a follow-up next week to walk through the matrix if you prefer a short run-through.

Thanks,
Marissa
